☄️ CoinDCX admits $15.99M loss days after denying hack claims 

🌐 CoinDCX has confirmed losing 15.99 million USDT through compromised wallet infrastructure after initially rejecting claims that nearly $16 million had been stolen from the Indian cryptocurrency exchange. The exchange said a failure in its automated deposit-sweeping service allowed cryptocurrency to accumulate at an address that customers continued using despite instructions to switch to newer wallets. CoinDCX absorbed the resulting loss and maintained that customer balances and active trading systems were not affected.

⚠️ The admission follows several days of disagreement between CoinDCX executives and blockchain investigators over suspicious transactions involving wallets linked to the exchange. On October 22, CoinDCX CEO Sumit Gupta rejected suggestions of another security breach, saying the flagged addresses belonged to infrastructure compromised in July 2025. He maintained that no funds had moved from current operational wallets into the addresses under scrutiny.

📊 However, the company’s latest statement confirms that deposits continued arriving at those addresses and that its own systems were responsible for transferring them to secure wallets when the automated service functioned correctly. CoinDCX said it noticed unusual activity on October 21 but discovered irregular fund movements the following day through blockchain records and community reports.

Lately, I've been interviewing AI Engineer candidates with 1–2 years of experience.

One thing surprised me.
Almost everyone can talk about RAG.
Almost everyone has built AI agents.

Most have used LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini.
But when the conversation moves beyond frameworks...
...that's where many interviews start to slow down.

I ask simple questions like:
"Why do embeddings work?"
"Why does chunk size affect retrieval?"
"Why does an attention mechanism matter?"
"What actually happens before an LLM generates the first token?"

The room usually goes quiet.
It made me realize something.
We're getting really good at building AI applications.

But we're slowly skipping the fundamentals that make those applications reliable.
AI tools can write code.
They can generate APIs.
They can even scaffold an entire project.

But they can't replace your understanding.
If retrieval quality drops...
If latency suddenly doubles...
If hallucinations increase...
If your AI agent gets stuck in a loop...

The solution isn't another framework.
It's understanding what's happening underneath.
Frameworks will change.
Models will change.
The fundamentals won't.

That's why, before every interview, I'd rather revise concepts like:
→ Transformers
→ Attention Mechanism
→ Embeddings
→ Tokenization
→ Vector Search
→ HTTP & APIs
→ System Design
→ Memory
→ Databases
→ Evaluation
→ Python fundamentals
These are the concepts that help you explain why something works, not just how to build it.

If you're preparing for AI Engineer interviews, don't spend all your time learning the next framework.
Spend some time strengthening the foundation that every framework is built on.

Markets are facing a pretty ugly combination right now.

Brent crude is already nearing $113. Tensions around Iran are rising again, and the market is starting to price in the risk of another escalation. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq continues to slide, investors are getting increasingly nervous about the cost of the AI boom, and Bitcoin is heading lower again alongside other risk assets.

And here’s one simple thing that’s important to understand. Almost everything in the global economy ultimately comes down to energy. More expensive oil means higher transportation costs, higher production costs, and more expensive goods and services. If oil stays above $110 for an extended period, it will give inflation another boost.

From there, a familiar chain reaction kicks in. Inflation rises, the Fed has a harder time cutting rates, borrowing costs stay high, and pressure on stocks and crypto intensifies. That’s exactly why the current rise in oil prices matters much more to the market than it might seem at first glance.

There’s another risk on the horizon: November 3, when the U.S. midterm elections take place. Reports are already emerging that another round of strikes on Iran could be under discussion specifically after the elections. That doesn’t mean the war will necessarily escalate. But after November 3, the political constraints on the White House could genuinely change, and the market is already starting to factor that in.

For us, the priority right now isn’t trying to call the bottom, but watching oil as one of the key risk indicators. As long as Brent stays above $110, any positive news for stocks or crypto could quickly be overshadowed by inflation concerns and high interest rates. On the other hand, a sustained decline in oil prices could be the first sign that pressure on the markets is starting to ease.

Veradermics has announced positive results from the Phase III trial of the VDPHL01 tablet for baldness.

Veradermics reported that the prolonged-release minoxidil tablet VDPHL01 met all primary and secondary endpoints in the Phase III study. The trial involved 536 men with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia.
According to the company's data, differences from placebo in hair counts, patient assessments, and investigator evaluations were seen as early as two months. By six months, non-vellus hair growth per square centimeter was 28.6 with once-daily dosing and 36.4 with twice-daily dosing compared to 6.6 with placebo. The developers stated that no serious adverse events related to the drug or cardiac events were reported.

The company plans to submit an application for approval to the FDA. If approved, this would be the first non-hormonal oral treatment for androgenetic alopecia.
